help.intro: A scene of about two minutes at a flat viewing in Leipzig: a young couple looks at a two-room flat, the landlady explains rent, extra costs and the missing kitchen, and the couple has to decide quickly because twelve other people want the flat too. The scene is invented; the numbers and customs are typical for a German city. You hear what you have just learnt: verbs with a fixed preposition (sich interessieren für, warten auf, sich kümmern um, denken an, sich freuen auf, fragen nach) with their question words (Worauf? Wofür?) and answers (darauf, dafür), and the word order of time, manner and place (Wir ziehen im März mit einem Transporter nach Leipzig: wann, wie, wo). Listen once for the whole scene, then once for the numbers.
help.tips[0].title: Verbs with a fixed preposition
help.tips[0].text: Many verbs always come with the same preposition: sich interessieren für (+ Akk.), warten auf (+ Akk.), sich freuen auf (+ Akk., future) / über (+ Akk., now), sich kümmern um (+ Akk.), denken an (+ Akk.), fragen nach (+ Dat.), sprechen mit (+ Dat.) / über (+ Akk.), sich bewerben um (+ Akk.). Asking about a thing: wo + preposition: Wofür interessieren Sie sich? Worauf warten Sie? (wor- before a vowel). Answering with a thing: da + preposition: Dafür. Darauf. For people: für wen? auf wen?
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: What are you interested in? In the two-room flat on the third floor. We have been waiting for it a long time.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Who looks after the garden? The caretaker looks after that.
help.tips[0].check.q: ____ warten Sie? Auf die Antwort der Vermieterin.
help.tips[0].check.why: warten auf → the question word is worauf (wo + r + auf before a vowel).
help.tips[1].title: Wann? Wie? Wo? in that order
help.tips[1].text: When a sentence has several pieces of information, German likes this order: time (wann), then manner / reason (wie, warum), then place (wo, wohin): Wir ziehen im März mit einem Transporter nach Leipzig. Sie kommen morgen mit dem Zug zur Besichtigung. If you put the time first, the verb follows it: Im März ziehen wir mit einem Transporter nach Leipzig. Short rule: te-ka-mo-lo (temporal, kausal, modal, lokal).
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: We can move to Leipzig with the whole household from 1 March because of the job.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The landlady will call you at home by phone this evening.
help.tips[1].check.why: Time (morgen), manner (mit dem Auto), place (nach Leipzig).
help.remember[0]: sich interessieren für → wofür? dafür; warten auf → worauf? darauf; sich kümmern um → worum? darum.
help.remember[1]: Order: wann, wie, wo: Wir ziehen im März mit einem Transporter nach Leipzig.
help.exam: Short scenes at a flat viewing or with a landlord, with numbers and conditions, are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: Two rooms, third floor, no kitchen, twelve other people interested: listen to a flat viewing and find out what the couple decides.
passageTranslation:
Landlady: Good evening, come in. You are Ms Brandt and Mr Özil?
Nora: Yes, exactly. Thank you for letting us come so quickly. We are very interested in the flat.
Landlady: I am glad. So: two rooms, 58 square metres, third floor, no lift. Here is the living room with balcony, there the bedroom, bathroom with window, and here the kitchen.
Tim: The kitchen is empty?
Landlady: Yes, the kitchen belongs to the old tenant. He moves out at the end of February. If you like, you can ask him afterwards whether he will sell it. He wants, I think, 800 euros.
Nora: And what does the flat cost?
Landlady: 690 euros cold. On top of that 180 euros extra costs for heating, water and rubbish, so 870 warm. Electricity and internet you pay yourselves. The deposit is three cold rents, 2,070 euros.
Tim: From when is the flat free?
Landlady: From 1 March. What are you waiting for, if I may ask? You live in Dresden now?
Nora: Yes. Tim starts a new job in Leipzig on 15 March. That is why we would like to move to Leipzig in March with a van.
Landlady: That fits. Who takes care of the paperwork with you? I need the last three pay slips, a confirmation from the old landlord that you always paid the rent, and your ID cards.
Tim: I will take care of that. I can send you everything by e-mail tomorrow.
Landlady: Good. I will tell you honestly: after you, twelve more people are coming today. I decide on Friday and then call.
Nora: We understand. We are really looking forward to the flat. The balcony is perfect.
Landlady: One more question: do you have pets?
Tim: A cat.
Landlady: A cat is fine. A dog would be more difficult. Then until Friday!
